h1: A project report for a cidery
title: Project Report for a Cidery | Craft Beer School
desc: What a cidery project report must show: fruit supply and seasons, juice yield, tank cycles, cash at harvest and the licence class for cider.
teaser: Cider is made once a year from fruit that arrives all at once. The report has to plan for that.
standfirst: A cidery buys its raw material in a short harvest window and sells the result across the year. That shape drives capacity, tanks and cash.
sections:
Beer can be brewed all year from stored malt. Cider depends on fruit that ripens in one season. The report must say which fruit, from where, from whom and on what terms. In India apple growing regions include Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Uttarakhand. Fruit quality and prices vary by variety and season. Cider apples differ from eating apples in sugar, acid and tannin. Many cideries blend. Say what you will use and what the supply contract looks like.

Fruit supply is also a risk. A poor crop or a price spike can change the economics in one year. A report should show how it would cope.

Volume starts with a yield assumption. A hypothetical: 100 tonnes of apples pressed at a 70 percent juice yield gives about 70 tonnes of juice, a little under 70,000 litres. Yield depends on variety, ripeness and the press, so test it on your own fruit and state your assumption. Then deduct losses in fermentation, racking and packaging. The volume that reaches the market is less than the juice pressed.

Pressing happens in a few weeks. Fermentation then runs cool, often at 12 to 18 °C, for weeks or months. A cidery therefore needs tanks to hold the whole harvest at once, not a smaller number cycling through. This is the opposite of a brewery. See capacity planning in a project report. A tank that is full once a year has a different return from one that cycles twenty times. Show tank utilisation honestly.

Fruit is paid for in the harvest weeks. Cider is sold over the following months. A neutral-unit illustration: you pay 120 for fruit within two months. Sales then return it at about 10 a month over the next twelve. Add packaging, labour and the loan. The peak funding need falls near harvest. It can be much bigger than the plant cost suggests. Model the cash monthly, not yearly. Say how the facility will be drawn and repaid.

How cider is classified varies. In some places it falls with wine, in others with beer or in its own class. In India, alcohol is a state subject, so licences, excise and some label rules differ by state and change. Describe the route at process level and confirm it with the regulator or a licensing adviser. Where alcohol is restricted, local law comes first.

Decide whether you sell dry, sweet, flavoured or sparkling cider and in which pack. Each changes cost and price. Cider is less known than beer in many markets, so the market section must show how you will build trade and consumer awareness. See the market section of a project report. Keep marketing responsible and within local advertising rules. Say how you will teach the trade to serve and store cider, since a warm shelf spoils a bottle.

Few cideries start at full scale. A sensible report shows a first harvest with a smaller press and fewer tanks, then adds capacity as sales prove out. Show the cost of each phase and what has to be true before the next starts. A trigger such as a stated sales volume held for three months is clearer than a date. Risks to name include a poor crop, a delayed licence, fermentation problems with a new fruit and slow trade acceptance. Give each a response.

Pressing leaves pomace, a large volume of wet fruit pulp. Say where it goes. It can be sold or used for feed or compost in some settings, but you must confirm the route and cost locally. If nobody collects it, a cidery pressing 100 tonnes of fruit has about 30 tonnes of pomace to move each season, on the 70 percent yield assumption above. Plan the trucks. Add effluent from cleaning, which carries sugars and fruit solids and needs treatment before it leaves the site. Then finish with the standard financial package. Methods are explained in NPV, IRR and payback.
faqs: Is a cidery report different from a brewery report?
Yes. The raw material is seasonal, the tanks must hold a whole harvest and cash needs peak at harvest.
What juice yield should I assume?
Test it on your own fruit and press. Yield varies by variety and ripeness, so state your assumption and its source.
Many cideries blend dessert and cider varieties. The right mix depends on your fruit supply and the style you want.
How is cider licensed in India?
Alcohol is a state subject, so classification and rules vary by state and change. Check with the regulator or a licensing adviser.
